objective: Stably order bounded dotted numeric versions by exact component values while preserving original strings and input ownership.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Stable comparison sorting and numeric parsing remain current.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Numeric release identifiers need component ordering rather than lexicographic order.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Comparator equality, missing defaults and defensive copying generalize.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Explicit digit/part bounds avoid conflating a lesson with full SemVer.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Unbounded Number conversion can silently lose ordering precision.

defects: Unbounded whole-number parts implied precision beyond Number’s exact domain.
Full SemVer versus dotted numeric versions and leading zeros were unstated.
Fresh empty/single arrays, long components and higher cardinality were not checked; hints overstated that native equality only accepts zero.
rationale: Retain the three correct sort/split/map strategies. Specify a numeric-only non-SemVer grammar, 1000 frozen-capable inputs, up to twenty decimal parts, leading zeros and each Number-exact value <=1000000000. Require fresh results for all sizes and original string retention. Explain the usual n log n comparison-sort model under bounded version length, without claiming a language-level sort bound. Add exact upper/leading-zero values, twenty-component distinctions, stable numeric ties, fresh empty/single arrays and 1000 descending versions.

defects: Whitespace-only titles could create empty nodes and alter later parentage.

rationale: Use an all-character title capture and ignore trimmed-empty titles before modifying the stack in all boards. Define column-zero ASCII-space headings, retained internal Unicode/trailing hashes, LF splitting and literal three-backtick toggle rules, with no full-Markdown claim. Replace the over-prescriptive regex hint with capture/stack guidance. Explain linear total text work, bounded six-level depth and fresh independent nodes/children. Add empty intermediate headings, internal U+2028, indentation/tab/seven-hash rejection, longer/open-ended fences, fresh repeated results and 5000 headings in 20000 code units.

objective: Recursively recolour a four-connected component on fresh independent row copies without mutating shared or frozen inputs.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Flood fill is a current foundational graph traversal.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Grid tools and image regions use connected-component traversal.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Visited marking, boundaries and deep-enough copying generalize.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: A 10x10 bound makes recursion practical in the supported runner.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Aliased rows, empty-string values and same-colour recursion can break correctness.

defects: Grid shape, valid indices, string domain and recursion bounds were unstated.
Copy independence for shared rows and empty colour strings lacked evidence.
Hints/comments described same-colour nontermination too categorically and conflated repeated calls with repeated processing.
rationale: Retain all correct recursive/map boards. Explicitly bound nonempty rectangular grids to 10x10, support frozen/shared rows and literal strings including empty, require independent copies of every row on all paths, and explain linear cell work/copy/stack space. Reword the visited-marking hint and same-colour comment to describe the actual cyclic risk. Add an empty-string replacement and a fully connected 100-cell shared/frozen-row grid, checking both changed and unchanged outputs for independent rows and preserved input. Larger images are explicitly outside the recursive exercise’s practical bound.

objective: Resolve literal own role names and bounded cyclic inheritance with recursive includes/some checks and per-call visited state.

relevanceRationale.presentDay: Graph-based permission inheritance remains a practical model.
relevanceRationale.practicalUtility: Admin interfaces often combine direct grants and inherited rules.
relevanceRationale.transferable: Cycle detection, own-key lookup and prefix boundaries transfer to authorization logic.
relevanceRationale.audienceFit: Bounded immutable graph data keeps the exercise focused rather than a full policy engine.
relevanceRationale.riskOutcome: Prototype roles, stale visited state and wildcard overreach can grant unintended permissions.

defects: Junior bypassed some for inheritance/roots; senior collected the graph before testing rather than implementing the requested recursive predicate/includes approach.
Nullable inheritance, immutable graphs, literal wildcard/name grammar and recursion/work bounds were unstated.
A fixed five-level cutoff passed the prior suite.
rationale: Align junior/senior to the recursive short-circuit predicate with includes, some and one visited Set per allowed call, retaining the correct reference. Define up to 100 immutable own roles, 1000 root names and 10000 total rule/link strings, bounded lengths, absent/null inheritance and literal names including __proto__/constructor. Only final :* is a prefix wildcard, including the empty suffix; bare * is literal. Explain linear aggregate graph/rule work under bounded strings and assumed average constant-time Set access (not a language-level bound). Add nonenumerable/null-prototype/frozen own role entries, ignored inherited grants, colon boundary and bare wildcard cases, 100-level cyclic/duplicate-edge reachability and repeated fresh-call checks.
